compare.item: Brennan’s Essential by Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut NV

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer
entries.same: A traditional method blend of Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay from Champagne, aged on its lees.
entries.different: Ours is Extra Brut, drier than the Brut most houses make, and labelled with the Brennan's name.

entries.label: The Piper-Heidsieck Brut magnum on our list
entries.same: The same Reims house and the same three grapes, dry and crisp.
entries.different: The magnum is Brut, so it may carry a little more sugar, and it pours a whole table.

compare.item: Pierre Sparr Brut Rosé Crémant d’Alsace NV

entries.label: The Codex sparkling wine primer
entries.same: Made by the traditional method, with the second fermentation in bottle, like Champagne.
entries.different: A Crémant d'Alsace rosé must be all Pinot Noir and comes from Alsace, not Champagne, at a friendlier price.

entries.label: Taittinger's rosé Champagne on our list
entries.same: Both are dry rosé sparkling wines with red berry fruit and a creamy mousse.
entries.different: The Taittinger is Champagne, from three grapes, coloured with still red wine; the Sparr is one grape from Alsace.

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer, vintage section
entries.same: Champagne made by the traditional method from Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
entries.different: Rare is a prestige vintage from one great year, aged about a decade on its lees, poured under Coravin.

entries.label: Pol Roger's vintage Blanc de Blancs
entries.same: Both are vintage Champagnes, Chardonnay-rich, long aged and fine.
entries.different: Pol Roger is all Chardonnay; Rare adds Pinot Noir and is a prestige cuvée with a jewelled bottle.

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer
entries.same: A non-vintage Brut Champagne blending Pinot Noir, Meunier and Chardonnay.
entries.different: Charles Lafitte is the tasting pour, a lighter, fresher everyday style from the Vranken-Pommery group.

entries.label: The Pommery rosé from the same group
entries.same: Both are Champagne from the Vranken-Pommery family of houses.
entries.different: The Pommery is a rosé, coloured with red wine; the Lafitte is white, poured on both tastings.

entries.label: The Codex Pacific Northwest primer
entries.same: Willamette Valley grapes, cool climate, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir at their best.
entries.different: Argyle turns them into traditional method sparkling wine, a speciality of the house since 1987.

entries.ref: Schramsberg ‘Blanc de Blancs’ North Coast 2021 (375 ml)
entries.label: Schramsberg, California's sparkling pioneer
entries.same: American traditional method sparkling wine, vintage dated, crisp and fine.
entries.different: Schramsberg is all Chardonnay from California; Argyle blends Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from Oregon.

entries.label: The Codex Riesling grape card
entries.same: Mosel Riesling: racy acidity, green apple, peach and slate.
entries.different: Berres is off-dry, about twenty grams of sugar, made to cool spice by the glass.

entries.label: Prüm's Kabinett on the bottle list
entries.same: Both are lightly sweet, low alcohol Middle Mosel Riesling from steep slate.
entries.different: Prüm is a famous single vineyard Kabinett; Berres is an old vines glass from Ürzig.

entries.label: The Codex Albariño grape card
entries.same: Rías Baixas Albariño: lemon, white peach and a saline snap.
entries.different: Ours is bottled young and unoaked by Familia Torres for freshness.

entries.ref: Do Ferreiro ‘Cepas Vellas’ Albariño Rías Baixas 2018
entries.label: Do Ferreiro's old vine Albariño
entries.same: Same grape, same coast, the same sea-spray freshness.
entries.different: Do Ferreiro is from very old vines with years in bottle, deeper and more textured.

compare.item: Famille Durand Val de Loire Sauvignon Blanc 2024

entries.label: The Codex Sauvignon Blanc grape card
entries.same: Loire Sauvignon Blanc: grapefruit, cut grass, a flinty note, bone dry.
entries.different: Ours names only the Val de Loire region, an everyday glass, not a village wine like Sancerre.

entries.label: Cotat's Sancerre on the bottle list
entries.same: Both are Loire Sauvignon Blanc with crisp acidity and herbs.
entries.different: Cotat is a cult single vineyard Sancerre, picked riper and richer, at a bottle price.

entries.label: The Codex Chardonnay grape card
entries.same: Chardonnay showing its place: lemon curd, baked apple and creamy texture.
entries.different: Ours is cool-climate California, ocean-cooled, so it stays fresh rather than heavy.

entries.label: Au Bon Climat in the Codex producers
entries.same: Sta. Rita Hills Chardonnay in a fresh, Burgundian-leaning style.
entries.different: Au Bon Climat is a single vineyard bottle; Gainey is the estate glass, rounder and easier.

entries.label: Domaine Leflaive in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same great Puligny estate and its biodynamic farming.
entries.different: This is its Mâconnais white from Verzé, lighter and gentler than its Puligny, poured by Coravin.

entries.label: Leflaive's Puligny on the bottle list
entries.same: One domaine, one style: citrus, white flowers and a chalky line.
entries.different: The Puligny is a Côte de Beaune village wine with years in bottle, deeper and more costly.

entries.label: The Codex Chardonnay grape card
entries.same: Mâcon Chardonnay: apple, citrus and gentle roundness.
entries.different: Mostly steel with a touch of old oak, from old limestone at Igé, so fresher than oaked styles.

entries.ref: Les Héritiers du Comte Lafon Mâcon-Milly-Lamartine 2023
entries.label: The Lafon family's Mâcon on the bottle list
entries.same: Both are village Mâcon Chardonnay, round and fresh.
entries.different: Lafon's comes from a Meursault family's southern estate; Fichet's is the dinner tasting pour.

entries.label: The Codex Southern France primer
entries.same: Provence's pale, dry rosé built on Grenache.
entries.different: Minuty is a cru classé from the hills above Saint-Tropez, poured by the glass.

entries.ref: Château d’Esclans ‘Whispering Angel’ Côtes de Provence Rosé 2024
entries.label: Whispering Angel on the bottle list
entries.same: Both are pale Côtes de Provence rosé: peach, strawberry, citrus.
entries.different: Whispering Angel adds Cinsault and Rolle, and comes by the bottle.

entries.label: The Codex Pinot Noir grape card
entries.same: Red Burgundy Pinot Noir: red cherry, raspberry, light tannin.
entries.different: A regional Bourgogne from a Mâconnais family, made to drink young by the glass.

entries.label: Faiveley's Bourgogne on the bottle list
entries.same: Both are regional red Burgundy, bright and fresh.
entries.different: Faiveley is a Nuits-Saint-Georges house blending across vineyards; Damien Martin a father and son domaine.

entries.label: Louis Jadot in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same great Beaune house and its Bacchus label.
entries.different: This is its Beaune Premier Cru, the dinner tasting red, silky with bright red fruit.

entries.ref: Bouchard Père & Fils ‘Clos de la Mousse’ Beaune Premier Cru 2022 (375 ml)
entries.label: Bouchard's Beaune Premier Cru half-bottle
entries.same: Both are Beaune Premier Cru Pinot Noir from great Beaune houses.
entries.different: Bouchard's is a walled monopole in a half-bottle; Jadot's is the tasting pour.

entries.label: The Codex Grenache grape card
entries.same: Grenache-led Southern Rhône red: ripe cherry, herbs and pepper.
entries.different: Ours is the dry red of an estate famous for sweet Muscat, with Syrah, lighter than Gigondas.

entries.label: The Raspail-Ay Gigondas half-bottle, next door
entries.same: Neighbouring villages under the Dentelles, Grenache with Syrah.
entries.different: Gigondas is fuller and firmer, the value step towards Châteauneuf.

compare.item: Domaine de Châteaumar ‘Cuvée Vincent’ Côtes du Rhône 2023

entries.label: The Codex Syrah grape card
entries.same: Syrah: black raspberry, black pepper and firm structure.
entries.different: Unusually for the south, ours is all Syrah, from fifty year old vines near Châteauneuf.

entries.label: Pegau's Châteauneuf, the step up with the filet
entries.same: Both are Southern Rhône reds from beside Châteauneuf, for the filet.
entries.different: Pegau is Grenache-led, warmer and more generous; Châteaumar is pure Syrah, peppery and soft.

entries.label: The Codex Bordeaux primer
entries.same: Left Bank Cabernet blend: cassis, plum and cedar.
entries.different: A Bordeaux Supérieur from Château d'Issan's vineyards outside the Margaux appellation, at a glass price.

entries.label: Château Talbot in the Codex producers
entries.same: Médoc Cabernet with Merlot, cassis and cedar.
entries.different: Talbot is a classified Saint-Julien growth with more depth; Moulin d'Issan is the easy glass.

entries.label: The Codex Barbera grape card
entries.same: Piemonte Barbera: high acidity, soft tannin, dark cherry.
entries.different: Ours comes from Asti, made with native yeasts and neutral oak, and named for local spirits.

entries.label: Inglenook in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same historic Rutherford estate founded in 1879.
entries.different: Rubicon is its flagship Bordeaux blend, here sixteen years old and poured by the glass.

entries.label: The Codex Cabernet Sauvignon grape card
entries.same: Cabernet-led: blackcurrant, cedar and tobacco.
entries.different: Age has softened Rubicon's tannin into earth and tobacco, unlike a young Napa Cabernet.

entries.label: The Codex Cabernet Sauvignon grape card
entries.same: Napa Cabernet: dark fruit, cocoa, firm structure.
entries.different: Coombsville is one of Napa's cooler corners, so it keeps freshness; it pours with the Rohan duck.

entries.label: Duckhorn's Napa Cabernet on the bottle list
entries.same: Both are young Napa Cabernet Sauvignon, structured and dark.
entries.different: Duckhorn blends valley vineyards and adds a little Merlot; Hobbs is a single cool district.

compare.item: Dr. Hermann ‘Erdener Prälat’ Riesling Auslese 2014 (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Riesling grape card
entries.same: Mosel Riesling with racy acidity and honeyed fruit.
entries.different: An Auslese, a selected harvest, sweet with apricot and honey, twelve years old.

entries.ref: Dönnhoff ‘Oberhäuser Brücke’ Riesling Auslese Goldkapsel 2023 (375 ml)
entries.label: Dönnhoff's gold capsule Auslese
entries.same: Both are sweet Riesling Auslese in half-bottles.
entries.different: Dönnhoff is young, from the Nahe, a richer gold capsule; Dr. Hermann has twelve years of age.

compare.item: Domaine La Tour Vieille Banyuls Reserva NV

entries.label: The Codex fortified wines primer
entries.same: Sweet wine fortified with grape spirit to keep its sugar.
entries.different: Banyuls is a French vin doux naturel of Grenache, aged oxidatively: fig, caramel and coffee.

entries.label: Niepoort's tawny Port
entries.same: Both are fortified, sweet and aged with air: walnut, caramel, coffee.
entries.different: Port is Portuguese, from Douro grapes; Banyuls is French Grenache, softer and less strong.

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer
entries.same: A non-vintage Brut Champagne.
entries.different: Drappier is from the Aube, Champagne's southern Côte des Bar, mostly Pinot Noir, in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Paul Bara Grand Cru Reserve Rosé Brut NV (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer, grower section
entries.same: Rosé Champagne by the traditional method.
entries.different: A grower's Grand Cru rosé from Bouzy, coloured with Bouzy red wine, in a half-bottle.

entries.label: Krug in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Reims house and its Grande Cuvée.
entries.different: Ours is a half-bottle, the edition inside to confirm with the sommelier.

compare.item: Billecart-Salmon ‘Brennan’s 80th Anniversary’ Brut Sous Bois NV (1.5 L magnum)

entries.label: Billecart-Salmon in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same family house of Mareuil-sur-Aÿ.
entries.different: This is its oak-fermented Sous Bois, in a magnum labelled for Brennan's 80th anniversary.

compare.item: Bollinger ‘Special Cuvée’ Brut NV (1.5 L magnum)

entries.label: Bollinger in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same rich, Pinot Noir-led house of Aÿ.
entries.different: Here its Special Cuvée in a magnum, two bottles in one for a table's toast.

entries.ref: Brennan’s Essential by Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut NV
entries.label: Our house Champagne by the glass
entries.same: The same Piper-Heidsieck house of Reims.
entries.different: This magnum is the house's own Brut, a touch rounder than the Extra Brut we pour by the glass.

compare.item: Taittinger ‘La Francaise’ Brut NV (3 L double magnum)

entries.label: Taittinger in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same family house of Reims and its Chardonnay-rich style.
entries.different: La Française in a double magnum, four bottles in one, the Champagne that tops the Flamingo.

compare.item: Mirabelle Brut Rosé North Coast NV

entries.label: Schramsberg in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Calistoga pioneer of traditional method sparkling wine.
entries.different: Mirabelle is its North Coast label, a non-vintage rosé, lighter in price.

entries.label: Pommery's rosé Champagne on the same page
entries.same: The same Vranken-Pommery group, dry sparkling rosé.
entries.different: Louis Pommery is Californian sparkling wine, not Champagne; the Pommery is Champagne from Reims.

entries.label: Moët & Chandon in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same great Épernay house.
entries.different: Its Imperial Rosé Brut: dry, coloured with red wine, unlike the sweet Nectar Impérial Rosé.

entries.ref: Moët & Chandon ‘Nectar Imperial’ Rosé Demi Sec NV
entries.label: Moët's sweet Nectar rosé on the bottle list
entries.same: One house, one pink colour, Pinot Noir-led.
entries.different: The Nectar is Demi-Sec, noticeably sweet, for dessert; the Imperial Rosé is dry.

entries.label: Taittinger in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same elegant Reims house.
entries.different: Its Prestige Rosé, coloured with still Pinot Noir, a pink sister to La Française.

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer
entries.same: Non-vintage rosé Champagne from Reims.
entries.different: Pommery made the first successful brut in 1874; this is its dry rosé, from the group behind Charles Lafitte.

compare.item: Chapel Down Rosé Brut Kent NV

entries.label: The Codex sparkling wine primer
entries.same: Traditional method sparkling rosé from chalk soils.
entries.different: English, from Kent, with bright cool weather acidity and red currant fruit.

entries.label: Ridgeview's English Brut
entries.same: Both are English traditional method sparkling wine on Champagne's chalk seam.
entries.different: Ridgeview's Bloomsbury is white and Chardonnay-led, from Sussex; Chapel Down's is a Kent rosé.

entries.label: The Codex sparkling wine primer
entries.same: The three Champagne grapes, made by the traditional method.
entries.different: From Sussex in England, Chardonnay-led, with green apple and crisp English acidity.

compare.item: Pierre Paillard Grand Cru ‘Les Parcelles XVIII’ Extra Brut NV

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer, grower section
entries.same: Grand Cru Champagne of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
entries.different: A family grower's own Bouzy parcels, Extra Brut, so very dry with real Pinot Noir body.

entries.ref: Paul Bara Grand Cru Reserve Rosé Brut NV (375 ml)
entries.label: Paul Bara, the other Bouzy grower
entries.same: Both are family growers in the Grand Cru village of Bouzy.
entries.different: Paul Bara's is a Brut rosé half-bottle; Paillard's is an Extra Brut white.

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer, grower section
entries.same: Rosé Champagne coloured with red Pinot Noir wine.
entries.different: A family grower in Merfy, north-west of Reims, savoury and chalky.

compare.item: Larmandier-Bernier Premier Cru ‘Longitude’ Extra Brut NV

entries.label: Larmandier-Bernier in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Vertus grower and its Côte des Blancs Chardonnay.
entries.different: Longitude is its Premier Cru Extra Brut, named for villages on one line of longitude.

entries.ref: Brennan’s Essential by Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut NV
entries.label: The same Champagne by the glass
entries.same: One wine: our Piper-Heidsieck Extra Brut house Champagne.
entries.different: This is the full bottle on the list, for a table; the glass pour is on the by-the-glass page.

compare.item: Moët & Chandon ‘Nectar Imperial’ Rosé Demi Sec NV

entries.label: Moët & Chandon in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Épernay house, Pinot Noir-led rosé.
entries.different: The Nectar Impérial Rosé is Demi-Sec, sweet: ripe strawberry and cream for dessert.

entries.label: Bollinger in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same family house of Aÿ.
entries.different: The Special Cuvée by the 750 ml bottle: rich, part oak fermented, built on reserve wines in magnum.

entries.label: Pol Roger in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Épernay family house, Churchill's Champagne.
entries.different: Its vintage Blanc de Blancs 2015, all Grand Cru Chardonnay, rather than its non-vintage Brut.

entries.label: Bollinger in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Pinot Noir house of Aÿ.
entries.different: PNTX20 is all Pinot Noir, a Blanc de Noirs led by Tauxières, built on the 2020 harvest.

entries.label: Billecart-Salmon in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same family house of Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, famous for rosé.
entries.different: Its prestige vintage rosé, named for Elisabeth Salmon, from 2009 with long age.

entries.label: The Rare 2012 we pour by the glass
entries.same: The same prestige Champagne, Chardonnay-led with Pinot Noir.
entries.different: This is the 2013 by the full bottle; the glass is the 2012 under Coravin.

entries.label: The Codex Gamay grape card
entries.same: Beaujolais Gamay: light, juicy red cherry and raspberry, soft tannin.
entries.different: A Beaujolais-Villages from Louis Jadot in a half-bottle, lighter than a cru such as Morgon.

entries.label: Lapierre's cru Morgon on the list
entries.same: Both are Gamay from northern Beaujolais, best with a light chill.
entries.different: Morgon is a cru, deeper and silkier, made with whole bunches by a natural wine pioneer.

compare.item: Chalk Hill Chardonnay Sonoma County 2021 (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Chardonnay grape card
entries.same: California Chardonnay: ripe pear, baked apple, creamy texture.
entries.different: Chalk Hill is Sonoma, round with toasty oak, in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Duckhorn Sauvignon Blanc North Coast 2023 (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Sauvignon Blanc grape card
entries.same: Sauvignon Blanc: citrus, grapefruit and fresh herbs, crisp.
entries.different: Duckhorn's North Coast style adds melon and a little roundness, friendlier than a flinty Loire.

entries.ref: Famille Durand Val de Loire Sauvignon Blanc 2024
entries.label: Our Loire Sauvignon by the glass
entries.same: The same grape, crisp and dry, lovely with herbs.
entries.different: The Durand is leaner and flintier from the Loire; Duckhorn is riper Californian fruit.

compare.item: Thierry et Pascale Matrot Bourgogne Blanc 2022 (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Chardonnay grape card
entries.same: White Burgundy Chardonnay: lemon, apple and a nutty roundness.
entries.different: A regional Bourgogne Blanc from a Meursault family, lighter and fresher than their village wines.

compare.item: Domaine Huet ‘Le Haut-Lieu’ Vouvray Sec 2019 (375 ml)

entries.label: Domaine Huet in the Codex producers
entries.same: The great Vouvray estate and its biodynamic Chenin Blanc.
entries.different: Le Haut-Lieu Sec 2019: dry, from its founding vineyard, with a few years of age.

entries.label: The Codex Grüner Veltliner grape card
entries.same: Classic Grüner: green apple, citrus and white pepper, dry.
entries.different: Bründlmayer's Terrassen comes from Kamptal terraces, in a half-bottle.

entries.label: The Codex Grenache grape card
entries.same: Grenache-led Southern Rhône: cherry, garrigue, pepper.
entries.different: Gigondas adds Syrah and firmer structure, a junior Châteauneuf in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Domaine Huet ‘Le Mont’ Vouvray Demi-Sec 2023 (375 ml)

entries.label: Domaine Huet in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same great Vouvray estate, all Chenin Blanc.
entries.different: Le Mont Demi-Sec: gently sweet, apple, pear and honey, with bright acidity.

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer
entries.same: Non-vintage Brut Champagne: apple, pear and brioche.
entries.different: Made by a large growers' cooperative at Chouilly, friendly and easy, in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Domaine Louis Michel ‘Montmains’ Chablis Premier Cru 2023 (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Chardonnay grape card, Chablis
entries.same: Chablis Chardonnay: lemon, green apple and oyster shell.
entries.different: Louis Michel uses no oak at all; Montmains is a Premier Cru, in a half-bottle.

entries.label: Dauvissat in the Codex producers
entries.same: Great Chablis from a reference family estate.
entries.different: Dauvissat uses some old oak and makes Grand Cru; Louis Michel uses only steel.

compare.item: Bergstrom ‘Reserve’ Pinot Noir Willamette Valley 2022 (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Pinot Noir grape card
entries.same: Pinot Noir: red cherry, cranberry and forest floor.
entries.different: Oregon's Willamette Valley gives brighter fruit than Burgundy; a Reserve in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Schramsberg ‘Blanc de Blancs’ North Coast 2021 (375 ml)

entries.label: Schramsberg in the Codex producers
entries.same: The Calistoga pioneer and its traditional method.
entries.different: The Blanc de Blancs, its first wine, poured at the 1972 Toast to Peace, here from 2021.

compare.item: Ridge Vineyards ‘Lytton Springs’ Dry Creek Valley 2021 (375 ml)

entries.label: Ridge Vineyards in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same old-vine Zinfandel champion.
entries.different: Lytton Springs is its Dry Creek field blend, in a half-bottle from 2021.

entries.label: The Codex Zinfandel grape card
entries.same: Zinfandel: brambly blackberry, pepper and spice.
entries.different: Ridge blends in Petite Sirah and Carignane from old field vines, for colour and freshness.

entries.label: The Heiligenstein in the Codex producers
entries.same: The famous Kamptal hill above Zöbing.
entries.different: This is Bründlmayer's dry Riesling from it, in a half-bottle: lime, peach, stony and smoky.

entries.label: Laurent-Perrier in the Codex producers
entries.same: The family house of Tours-sur-Marne.
entries.different: Harmony is its Demi-Sec, gently sweet, for dessert, in a half-bottle.

entries.label: The Codex Zinfandel grape card
entries.same: Zinfandel's ripe dark fruit and spice.
entries.different: Essence is late harvest and sweet, from shrivelled grapes, made only in rare years.

compare.item: Bouchard Père & Fils ‘Clos de la Mousse’ Beaune Premier Cru 2022 (375 ml)

entries.label: Bouchard Père et Fils in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same historic Beaune house.
entries.different: The Clos de la Mousse is its walled Beaune Premier Cru monopole, in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Ridge Vineyards ‘Estate’ Cabernet Sauvignon Santa Cruz Mountains 2020 (375 ml)

entries.label: Monte Bello in the Codex producers
entries.same: Ridge's mountain Cabernet country in the Santa Cruz Mountains.
entries.different: The Estate comes from vineyards around Monte Bello, not the flagship itself, in a half-bottle.

entries.label: Louis Jadot in the Codex producers
entries.same: The great Beaune house.
entries.different: Its village Meursault: buttery, nutty Chardonnay from barrel, in a half-bottle.

compare.item: Veuve Fourny et Fils Premier Cru Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut NV (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer, grower section
entries.same: Blanc de Blancs Champagne from the Côte des Blancs.
entries.different: A Vertus family grower's Premier Cru, Extra Brut, bone dry, in a half-bottle.

entries.label: Larmandier-Bernier, also of Vertus
entries.same: Both are Vertus growers making Extra Brut Blanc de Blancs.
entries.different: Larmandier-Bernier's Longitude is a full bottle; Veuve Fourny's is the half-bottle.

compare.item: La Cigarrera Manzanilla Sanlúcar de Barrameda NV (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex fortified wines primer, sherry
entries.same: Sherry: Palomino, fortified and aged in a solera.
entries.different: Manzanilla is the lightest style, aged under flor in Sanlúcar's sea air, bone dry and salty.

entries.label: Dow's in the Codex producers
entries.same: The same Symington Port house.
entries.different: Its declared Vintage Port 2000 in a half-bottle, on the drier side of Port.

entries.label: Graham's from the same year
entries.same: Same family, same declared vintage, same grapes.
entries.different: Graham's is richer and riper; Dow's drier. A lesson in house style.

entries.label: Niepoort in the Codex producers
entries.same: The Dutch-origin family Port house.
entries.different: A Colheita, a single harvest tawny from 1997, aged in cask, no decanting needed.

compare.item: Veuve Fourny et Fils Premier Cru Rosé Brut NV (375 ml)

entries.label: The Codex Champagne primer, grower section
entries.same: Rosé Champagne from the Côte des Blancs.
entries.different: A Vertus grower's Premier Cru rosé, light and bright, in a half-bottle.
